## Design constraints the context pass settled (inputs for the planner, not questions)

1. **Card key paths vary** — `reproducibility_card.git_commit`,
   `note.reproducibility_card.git_commit`, and `repro.git_commit` all occur
   within one issue. A recursive key search is required; a fixed dotted path
   would silently miss cards.
2. **Cards routinely live on an unmerged issue branch.** `eval_results/issue_2162`
   on `main` contains no cards at all; every card above is reachable only at
   `origin/issue-2162`. Absent-cards must degrade (skip/WARN), never FAIL.
3. **`git_commit` is not always a usable SHA.** `eval_results/issue_1768/on_target/upload_done.json`
   records `git_commit: "unknown"`; `judge_summary.json` records an abbreviated
   `6eec51c7` plus `git_dirty: true` with dirty paths. Skip `unknown`,
   prefix-match abbreviations, and treat a dirty card as non-authoritative.
4. **Reports cite SHAs abbreviated with an ellipsis** (`ba3485b619…`, 10 hex +
   U+2026), so the row matcher cannot assume 40-hex.
5. **Check (a) needs a pin source, and the report does not always give one
   inline.** The git-home claim at line 37 carries no SHA; line 114 supplies the
   branch and a tip SHA separately. Resolving which pin a claim is made against
   is the single genuinely open design question — and per the body's own
   instruction it resolves toward under-firing: only assert when a pin is
   unambiguously resolvable, else skip with a WARN.

None of the five is blocking: each has a conservative default that satisfies the
body's stated preference, and the planner owns the exact shape.
Clarifier All-clear; body is a complete spec, all five design constraints resolved from the repo.

## Applied — Must-Fix 1 (methodology lens): check (a) does NOT catch its founding incident

The sharpest finding of the round, and it reshaped what the deliverable is allowed
to claim. #2162's round-1 defective sentence claimed scores+items were committed
under the PARENT `eval_results/issue_2162/judge/` — which holds **82 blobs** at
`20fcef9c28`. The task body's own falsifiability rule (`ls-tree -r <pin> -- <path>`
returning >= 1 blob) therefore **PASSES that sentence**. Two independent witnesses
fix the parent-path wording: task body line 31, and the clarifier's pre-correction
record of report line 37 (`tasks/planning/2191/events.jsonl` line 2, taken 19:19,
before the #2162 session's in-place fix at ~19:25). That same clarifier record
notes the round-1 line carried **no same-line pin** — a second, independent reason
the check could at most have WARNed. v1 knew this class existed but framed it as a
hypothetical ("if the verbatim round-1 sentence named only the non-empty `judge/`
dir..."); the plan's own two cited sources resolve the "if" AGAINST the plan.

Fix applied (documentation + one pinned test; NO matcher change):
- §0.0 gains an explicit "What check (a) will NOT catch" bullet.
- §3 H1 split into H1a (check (b), faithful reconstruction) / H1b (check (a),
  empty-path FORM, with the witnessed sentence a documented PASS).
- §4.1 "named residue" rewritten: states plainly that check (a) is SILENT (clean
  PASS, not even WARN) on the defect that motivated it, with both witnesses cited.
- §6 criterion 1 relabelled to the EMPTY-PATH FORM and its fixture explicitly
  declared NOT a faithful reconstruction of the witnessed sentence.
- §6 criterion 1-bis ADDED: a test asserting the witnessed parent-path form returns
  `passed=True, is_warn=False`, docstring naming it the incident's witnessed shape
  and the reason it is not caught. Framed as a regression gate in the UNDER-FIRE
  direction: if it ever FAILs, the matcher has been broadened past sanctioned scope.
- §0 controls line + §5 conditions table corrected for internal consistency.

Broadening was REJECTED, on the body's own instruction: any mechanical subset rule
(mapping claim nouns like "scores"/"items" to filename tokens under the path) is
free-text semantics with a live false-FAIL channel — "gate reports committed under
`judge/`" would FAIL though correct.

## Applied — Must-Fix 2 (alternatives lens): b1 needs a mode split

Check (b1)'s FAIL compares a FROZEN report against an EXTERNAL MUTABLE reference
set: the card set under `eval_results/issue_<N>/**` keeps growing after authoring,
so any later follow-up round writing one more full-40-hex non-dirty card makes a
previously-PASSing, UNCHANGED report FAIL at `--mode promote` — blocking promotion
of a good result, the task body's named worst outcome. v1's §2 already cited
`_check_pin_blob_identity` as this check's model precisely FOR its mode-split
degrade ladder, but v1's signature did not honor it.

Fix applied: `mode` threaded into `check_code_sha_cards` (signature + §4.3 wiring);
b1 is FAIL at `generation`, `is_warn=True` at `promote`; b2/b3 stay WARN in both.
Pinned by a new criterion-5 test row. Check (a) deliberately takes NO mode — its
FAIL condition is time-stable and matches the model check's `does not contain
{path}` arm, which carries no mode branch (FAIL in both modes). Orchestrator
re-verified both facts directly against the live file before applying.

## Applied — Must-Fix 3 (alternatives lens): check (a) negation guard too narrow

v1 guarded only two exact lookbehinds, defeated by every natural negation variant
("nothing is committed under X", "isn't/wasn't in git under X", "rather
than / instead of in git under X", "never landed in git under X", "no longer
committed under X"). Each would FAIL a CORRECT sentence when the line also carries
a resolvable pin and an empty path — realistic, not contrived, because the FAIL
message itself teaches authors to reword false git-home claims into HF-home
sentences that naturally retain the empty git path for contrast.

Fix applied: replaced the lookbehinds with a preceding-window negation scan
(`_NEGATION_WINDOW_CHARS = 40`, `_NEGATION_TOKENS` tuple); §4.1's over-claiming
"Negated claims" not-fire bullet corrected; criterion 5 gains one fixture row per
variant PLUS an over-suppression guard row (a "not" EARLIER than the window must
still FAIL, so the guard cannot silently swallow genuine defects in long sentences).

## Adjudicated — cross-critic split on b3 (pairing WARN): RETAINED

The two critics disagreed. Alternatives recommended DROPPING b3 (silent on the
incident's own defective segment, zero confirmed catches, ungrounded stopword set).
Methodology independently analysed b3's residue as narrower than it looks (a
backwards pairing touching >= 1 resolvable label — margin, stage2 — does WARN; only
swaps confined to unresolvable-label phases escape) and treated it as load-bearing.

Decision: **KEEP, with the stopword set pinned by test** — the drop-recommending
critic's own stated fallback condition. Rationale: b3 is the ONLY leg that can catch
MISPAIRING (a row citing every correct card SHA but paired to the wrong phases),
which is exactly what the task body asked check (b) to do, and which b1's coverage
direction provably cannot see. b3 is WARN-only in both modes, so the body's named
worst outcome is structurally unreachable — retention costs bounded noise, dropping
costs a permanent blind spot on the body's literal ask. Recorded in §11.
